analysis:
This PR changes only docs/reference/protocol-messages.md. Visible head units 7 (lines 1-325) and 8 (lines 326-582) contain only the date bump at line 3 as a changed line; the other changed ranges (854, 1208, 1355-1380, 1470-1472) fall outside the supplied head text. The patch excerpt adds a Swift-only optional `detail` field on `model_autopilot_status` (line 854) and a Swift-only `hold_seconds` field on the autopilot command (line 1208), but the surrounding source is not supplied.

No code, key handling, or authorization logic changes in the supplied text. The visible content describes the App Attest endpoint-resume contract (lines 47-109), the provider drain barrier (111-170), and message inventory/field tables. These are consistent with TB-002, TB-011, T-053, and A-008/A-016. They state that resume is not a bearer grant, that the provider does not independently validate the coordinator's record/account policy, and that the backend owns authorization. That stated delegation is a pre-existing contract, not a new regression.

The new `detail` field is described as consent-gated and as not an authorization or capacity signal. `hold_seconds` is documented as a placement hold (0...86400 range, invalid_command without load_model_id). Neither is evidenced as widening provider attack surface, but I could not verify the implementation or the coordinator bounds. Remaining questions for later review:
- whether the Swift `detail` emission leaks anything sensitive beyond the stated busy-reason enum;
- whether the `hold_seconds` bound is enforced coordinator-side;
- the unseen tail of the patch (lines 1355-1380 and 1470-1472).

No concrete security finding is supported by the visible evidence. I set needs_deeper_review because most changed ranges are outside the supplied units.
